# hands/telegram

the only holder of Teeny's Telegram bot token.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/telegram <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): send
- Job (writes state or calls the core): ingest [--max N]; queue [--status S]
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: whoami; chats

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `whoami` | R | The bot's id and username, whether it reads all group messages (privacy mode off), and the owners. |
| `ingest [--max N]` | J | Reads new updates from a cursor (`telegram_cursor`), each text message a row in `telegram_messages`, screened by the inbound guard. |
| `chats` | R | The chats Teeny is in or was written to from. |
| `queue [--status S]` | J | The intake and what became of each message. |
| `send` | A | `{chat_id, text, reply_to?}`. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `chats`, `ingest`, `queue`, `send`, `whoami`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--max`, `--status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/telegram <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
